findings.title: Producer preserved closure is skipped before launch
findings.detail: All five frozen producer plans contain808 preserved_files records. V1 verifies preserved only, omitting that closure until the frozen child later verifies it.
findings.required_successor: Verify both preserved_files and preserved, reconcile duplicates exactly, before activation or process launch.

findings.title: Provisional positive terminal is consumable after failed reserve validation
findings.detail: V1 writes full_resource_accepted=true to the final normalized path before post-write validation. A failed reserve check produces exit1/accepted_for_metadata_finalization=false, but the frozen finalizer and scientific qualification consume the terminal fields without requiring that observation. Manual caller obedience is needed to avoid stale positive use.
findings.required_successor: Publish no final accepted normalized path until already-written bytes and post-serialization clocks/peaks pass. Atomically promote immutable provisional bytes, and bind a successful post observation in downstream ROOT qualification/report metadata before invoking frozen finalizer.

findings.title: Post-serialization memory and final observer are not checked
findings.detail: Conservative memory is computed before terminal JSON serialization; post validation tests time only. The final process_table subprocess is reaped after the last observer_peak update and its individual usage is not separately retained. A larger ROOT serialization peak or final observer can evade the stored positive resource test.
findings.required_successor: Record terminal usage for each ROOT ps observer and recheck ROOT and observer-inclusive memory after provisional receipt serialization/close, as well as time, before promotion.

findings.title: Producer inner observer contribution lacks a separate bound
findings.detail: The frozen producer supervisor explicitly labels ps observer RSS omitted; its own+child kernel peak uses a maximum over reaped children. ROOT max(inner_peak,owner_peak,owned_RSS) is not a sum including an inner ps that may never be sampled. This is a retrospective estimate, not an observer-complete estimate by source construction.
findings.required_successor: Add an explicit sound inner-observer contribution. ROOT proposed adding the supervisor kernel_child_peak_bytes upper bound for its one sequential observer; this conservatively double-counts the worker and may correctly force resource UNKNOWN. Do not relax budgets or silently discard this charge.

findings.title: Exact selected plan/schema is not directly bound to reviewed manifest
findings.detail: V1 checks selector and each self-declared plan record, but does not check exact plan schema or selected producer plan raw pin against the reviewed source manifest. Self-declared closure consistency does not prove that the configuration being launched is the frozen selector plan.
findings.required_successor: For preparation, match the entire raw selected plan to the reviewed V3 manifest input role; for static, require exact frozen actual-static schema/stage/ROOT-only flags plus review-linked immutable plan and nested receipt bindings. Bind launch and activation to those exact bytes.

findings.title: Cleanup can leave unobserved or zero-RSS owned descendants unconfirmed
findings.detail: PGID is collected but unused. Tracking is based on sampled PPID descendants and retained PIDs; a quickly reparented descendant can be missed. Survivors filter discards zero-RSS entries, and SIGKILL is followed by no fresh absence/terminal check. This does not create a positive receipt when survivors are found, but does not establish clean terminal ownership after a failure.
findings.required_successor: Use known receipt worker/supervisor PIDs and owned process groups as well as lineage; distinguish live processes from zombies without treating RSS0 as absence; preserve an explicit unconfirmed-cleanup failure and stop all progression if full terminal cleanup cannot be established.

findings.title: Clock scope starts at main and ends at receipt bytes
findings.detail: V1 main timer excludes Python startup/module imports; post-observation write and dispatcher exit are explicitly excluded. Scientific owners/workers are terminal before this metadata work, so the scope can be stated, but it is not an independent measurement of the entire dispatcher process lifetime.
findings.required_successor: Keep this scope explicit and charge external ROOT launch/import/exit observations separately if reporting the complete ROOT process lifetime. Do not label a main-only interval as an externally measured full process clock.

positive_alignment: Five literal selectors and two declared phases; expected60/180-second and512MiB ceiling choices.
Exclusive x-mode receipt/stdout/stderr/activation outputs and immutable one-shot namespaces.
Actual immediate child termination is consumed through wait4; passed preparation/static paths require frozen inner worker/owner reaping statuses.
Runtime/observer byte identities and reviewed source pins are checked.
Post-write clock observation exists; budget or infrastructure failure returns nonzero and is not a theorem failure.
ROOT_proposed_successor_assessment: Exclusive provisional full receipt bytes, post-serialization time+memory checks, atomic hard-link promotion only after success, successful post-observation pin before finalization, and explicit inner observer bound addressF2/F3/F4 if implemented exactly. Preserve V1 and use a fresh successor namespace; also fixF1/F5 and retain cleanup/scope gaps until resolved.
